docs.text: For #TidesOutTuesday today. I confess that Lake Ontario doesn't have much in the way of tides but the water does slosh around from one end to the other making sort of tides. Anyway, that's my story and I'm sticking to it 😀 #Photography #EastCoastKin
#TidesOutTuesday. Well it is a lake, so not really a tide, but Lake Ontario does have little tides...sort of... #Photography #EastCoastKin

We don't have tides on Lake Erie, but we do have something called a seiche, which is when the wind pushes all our water somewhere else. It looks a lot like the tide is out, including gulls standing on newly revealed rocks, but there aren't that many interesting shells. 🌿
In the #GreatLakes, we don't have tides, but we do have seiches (oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/seiche...) which are driven by winds

Technically we *do* have tides in the #GreatLakes, they're just really, really, really small - less than 5 cm at the max - and overshadowed by seiches and other fluctuations oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/gltide...
If Lake Michigan had a low tide, I imagine this is what it would look like. This might be part of a seiche in action. That water that isn't here needs to go somewhere 😋
The Great Lakes experience small tides twice a day, but the water level change is usually less than 5 centimeters.
I grew up on the Great Lakes, and recently visited a place with tides (New Brunswick) for the first time in my life. Mind bending, to have the water just ... change drastically every day.
No, Lake Superior is classified as “non-tidal". This is just wind and waves.
I don't know but I have learned from this here bsky that lake michigan has some serious undertow/rip tides
The Great Lakes have tides of less than 5cm; waves and barometric changes provide much greater variation in depth. oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/gltide...

Freshwater estuaries are semi-enclosed areas of #GreatLakes where river/stream water mixes with lake water per NOAA’s classification of estuaries. You have tides and I have seiches?

Ah, yeah, Lake Superior does have tides. It is out there having tides while being not saline at all. Gestures broadly. Sir what are you even up to over there.

And I mean I only (mostly jokingly) opened this can of worms because Lake Superior gets referred to as a sea a lot, and it turns out there isn't any one strict geological definition. Superior is huge and has significant waves, etc. But no tides, no salt. It's kind of its own thing!
